name: Pharmacovigilance processing of one individual case safety report (postmarketing)
summary: When a patient, doctor, pharmacist or partner tells a drug company about a side effect, the company must record it as an individual case safety report, judge whether it is valid and serious, enter and code it in a safety database, write a narrative, check its quality and have a physician review it. Serious unexpected cases must reach FDA electronically within 15 calendar days of first receipt, and the company must chase missing information. Most work is manual reading and re-keying of unstructured reports, with queues at data entry, quality review and medical review, and many reporters never answer follow-up requests.

baseline.org_archetype: A mid-size US pharmaceutical company with about ten marketed products, an in-house pharmacovigilance operations team (part of the data entry often outsourced) and a commercial safety database.
baseline.notes: Postmarketing spontaneous, patient support program and solicited reports; clinical trial (IND) safety reports and literature screening are out of scope. US FDA rules are used; EU timelines are mentioned only where they shape the work.

unit_of_work: one individual case safety report (initial report or follow-up version)
trigger: Any employee, vendor or partner of the company receives information about an adverse event with one of its products.
end_state: The case is submitted to FDA within the deadline and follow-up attempts are completed, or it is completed for periodic reporting, closed as not valid, or merged as a duplicate.

volume.seasonality: Spikes after media coverage, label changes and new patient support programs.

evidence.note: Estimate for a mid-size company with about ten marketed products.

triggered_by.from: Patient support and market research programs
Health professionals and patients writing directly (email, fax, web form)

produces.object: case under the safety data exchange agreement

systems.name: Safety database (case management system such as Argus or ARISg)
Safety intake mailbox, fax and call center transfer
MedDRA and WHODrug coding dictionaries and browsers
FDA Electronic Submissions Gateway (E2B ICSR transmission and acknowledgements)
Current product labeling (US prescribing information) and reference safety information
Partner safety data exchange (secure email or SFTP)
Compliance tracking spreadsheet and CAPA system

steps.name: Log the report and set Day 0
steps.description: The intake associate opens the report from the safety mailbox, fax, call center or affiliate transfer, records the date the company first received it as Day 0, creates a case shell in the safety database and attaches the source documents.
inputs: source report (email, fax, call note, form)

error.defect_description: Wrong Day 0 or source attachment missing.

control.basis: 21 CFR 314.80(c)(1): the 15 calendar day clock starts at initial receipt of the information by the applicant.

evidence.note: Intake is the first case processing activity; times are estimates.

steps.name: Translate the foreign-language source
steps.description: A translation vendor receives the source document through a secure portal, translates it into English, and the translation is attached to the case before duplicate search and data entry.

error.defect_description: Translation error in event or dose.

evidence.note: Common for global companies; share and time are estimates.

steps.name: Search for duplicates
steps.description: The intake associate searches the safety database by patient initials, age or birth date, product, event and reporter to decide whether the report is new, follow-up to an existing case, or a duplicate of one already received from another channel.

error.defect_description: Duplicate missed or follow-up opened as a new case.

control.basis: EU GVP Module VI Addendum I on duplicate management, and company SOP.

evidence.note: Duplicate management is covered by GVP Module VI Addendum I; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Triage validity and seriousness
steps.description: A drug safety associate checks the four minimum criteria (identifiable patient, identifiable reporter, suspect product and adverse event), judges seriousness against the regulatory definitions, flags whether the event appears in the label, and sets the priority and due date.

error.defect_description: Seriousness missed, putting a 15-day case in the routine queue.

control.basis: 21 CFR 314.80(a) definitions of serious and unexpected; ICH E2D minimum criteria for a valid case.

evidence.note: Definitions and the four validity elements are stated in the sources; ICH E2D governs post-approval case management; shares are estimates.

steps.name: Ask the reporter for minimum information
steps.description: The associate sends a letter, email or call to the reporter asking for the missing patient, product or event details, and diarizes the case for the response.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the reporter's reply
steps.description: The case is diarized while the consumer or health professional decides whether to answer the request for minimum information; many never reply, and the case is closed as not valid after the diary date.

next.condition: no reply; closed as not valid

evidence.note: Response share and time are estimates.

steps.name: Enter the serious case in full
steps.description: The associate keys patient details, medical history, suspect and concomitant products with doses and dates, events with onset and outcome, lab results and reporter details from the source documents into the safety database fields.

error.defect_description: Field omitted or mis-keyed (dates, doses, outcome).

evidence.note: Manual extraction from unstructured sources is the main case processing cost; times are estimates.

steps.name: Code events, history and products
steps.description: The associate codes each event, indication and history item to a MedDRA lowest level term and each product to WHODrug, checking the auto-suggested terms against the reporter's words.

error.defect_description: Term too general or too specific for the verbatim.

control.basis: MedDRA coding and ICH E2B data structure required for electronic ICSRs to FDA (21 CFR 314.80(g)).

evidence.note: FAERS codes events in MedDRA and follows E2B; times are estimates.

steps.name: Write the case narrative
steps.description: The associate writes a chronological narrative of the case from the source, following the company template: patient, history, product exposure, event course, treatment, outcome and reporter comments.

error.defect_description: Narrative omits or contradicts coded data.

evidence.note: Standard ICSR component; times are estimates.

steps.name: Quality check against the source
steps.description: A senior associate compares every entered field, code and the narrative with the source documents, records findings in the quality log and returns the case for correction when errors are found.

control.basis: Company PV quality system SOP requiring independent quality review of serious cases before submission.

evidence.note: Common practice; rework shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Medical review of seriousness, expectedness and causality
steps.description: The safety physician reviews the case and narrative, confirms seriousness and whether the event is listed in the current label, assesses causality, adds a company comment and approves the case or sends it back.

control.basis: Company PV SOP requiring physician medical review of serious cases; expectedness judged against current labeling per 21 CFR 314.80(a).

evidence.note: Evaluation is a core activity; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Determine reportability and destinations
steps.description: The reporting specialist reviews the destinations the safety database rules propose (FDA 15-day report, partners, other authorities) against seriousness, expectedness and source, confirms due dates and schedules the reports.

error.defect_description: Destination missed or wrong due date.

evidence.note: Reportability rules from the regulation; share is an estimate.

steps.name: Generate and send the E2B report
steps.description: The specialist generates the E2B ICSR file from the safety database, checks it against the case, and transmits it to FDA through the Electronic Submissions Gateway.

control.basis: 21 CFR 314.80(c)(1)(i) 15-day Alert report and 314.80(g) electronic submission format.

evidence.note: Deadline and format rule from the regulation; times are estimates.

steps.name: Check the acknowledgement
steps.description: The specialist checks the gateway and business-rule acknowledgements, records the submission date in the case and the compliance tracker, and re-sends any rejected file.

next.condition: accepted; partners must receive the case

evidence.note: Rejection and late shares are estimates.

steps.name: Investigate a late submission
steps.description: The compliance specialist records the late case, finds the cause (late transfer from an affiliate, missed seriousness, backlog) and opens or links a corrective and preventive action.

control.basis: PV quality system compliance monitoring of 15-day timeliness, reviewed in FDA inspections.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Send the case to partners
steps.description: Under safety data exchange agreements, the specialist sends the case to licensing or co-marketing partners by secure email or E2B within the agreed timelines and logs the transfer.

error.defect_description: Partner not sent the case in time.

control.basis: Safety data exchange agreement with each partner.

evidence.note: Common for licensed products; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Decide on and send follow-up questions
steps.description: The associate lists missing information that matters for assessment (lab values, dechallenge, outcome) and sends a targeted follow-up letter or questionnaire to the reporter.

control.basis: 21 CFR 314.80(c)(1)(ii): promptly investigate 15-day reports and submit follow-up within 15 days of new information.

evidence.note: Follow-up is a core activity; share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the follow-up reply
steps.description: The case is diarized while the reporter decides whether to answer the follow-up questions; any reply is logged as a new version of the same case with its own Day 0 for the 15-day follow-up clock.

next.condition: new information received; processed as a follow-up version

evidence.note: Response share and time are estimates.

steps.name: Send a second request and close the case
steps.description: After the diary date the associate sends a second request; when there is still no answer the case is closed with the follow-up attempts documented.

evidence.note: Common practice of two or three attempts; times are estimates.

steps.name: Enter the nonserious case
steps.description: The associate keys the main fields for the nonserious case, with a shorter narrative, at lower priority than serious cases.

evidence.note: Lower priority because nonserious cases go to periodic reports; times are estimates.

steps.name: Code the nonserious case
steps.description: The associate codes each event and indication to a MedDRA lowest level term and each product to WHODrug, checking the terms the safety database suggests against the reporter's verbatim text.

evidence.note: Coding per MedDRA and WHODrug; sample share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Sample quality check
steps.description: A senior associate checks a sample of nonserious cases field by field against the source documents, records findings in the quality log and returns cases with errors for correction.

control.basis: Company PV quality system SOP for sample-based review of nonserious cases.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Complete the case for periodic reporting
steps.description: The associate marks the case complete so it is included as an ICSR in the next periodic report and is available for signal detection.

control.basis: 21 CFR 314.80(c)(2): nonserious and serious expected ICSRs are submitted with the periodic report, quarterly for three years after approval and annually after that.

evidence.note: Periodic reporting rule from the regulation; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Not valid, query for minimum information
exceptions.description: A criterion is missing; the reporter is asked and most cases close as not valid after no reply.

exceptions.name: Duplicate
exceptions.description: The same event arrives from two channels and is merged.

exceptions.name: Quality rework
exceptions.description: The quality reviewer returns data entry or narrative errors before medical review.

exceptions.name: Late 15-day report
exceptions.description: The report reaches FDA after day 15 and a root cause and CAPA are recorded.

exceptions.name: Follow-up information
exceptions.description: The reporter answers and the new version is processed and resubmitted as a follow-up report.

exceptions.name: Foreign-language source
exceptions.description: The source is translated before data entry.

exceptions.name: Seriousness upgraded at medical review
exceptions.description: A case triaged as nonserious is upgraded, compressing the remaining time to the 15-day deadline.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from Day 0 to case closure, including follow-up attempts
benchmarks.population: Postmarketing ICSRs at a mid-size drug company

evidence.note: Anchored on the 15-day deadline for serious unexpected cases (companies aim to submit well before day 15) and lower priority for cases reported only in periodic reports; follow-up waits are estimates.

benchmarks.population: Serious and unexpected postmarketing experiences, US
PVNet benchmark cited by Pfizer authors

benchmarks.unit: share of cases with 8 or 9 of 9 entities correct

pain_points.description: Case processing is mostly manual reading and re-keying of unstructured reports, and takes most of the PV budget.
Serious cases wait in queues for quality review and physician review while the 15-day clock runs.

evidence.note: Queue lengths are estimates.

pain_points.description: The same event arrives through several channels and must be found and merged.
Many reporters never answer follow-up requests, so cases close incomplete after several attempts.

evidence.note: Common experience; estimate.

pain_points.description: Late transfers from affiliates and missed seriousness at triage cause late 15-day reports.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: 21 CFR 314.80 Postmarketing reporting of adverse drug experiences
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Serious and unexpected experiences reported as 15-day Alert reports no later than 15 calendar days from initial receipt; prompt investigation and follow-up reports within 15 days of new information; periodic reports quarterly for 3 years then annually, containing serious expected and nonserious ICSRs; electronic submission required; records kept 10 years; definitions of serious and unexpected.

sources.title: Innovation in Pharmacovigilance: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Adverse Event Case Processing
sources.supports: Case processing can take up to two-thirds of internal PV resources (PVNet benchmark) and most of the PV budget with outsourcing; activities are intake, evaluation, follow-up and distribution; a valid case needs an adverse event, suspect drug, patient and reporter; vendor AI extraction pilots reached composite F1 of 0.52 to 0.74 and 13 to 34 percent case-level completeness.

sources.title: FDA Adverse Event Monitoring System (AEMS), formerly FAERS
sources.supports: FAERS holds adverse event, medication error and product quality reports for postmarketing surveillance; events are coded with MedDRA; the database structure follows ICH E2B.

sources.title: Good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP)
sources.supports: GVP Module VI (Rev. 2, effective 22 November 2017) covers collection, management and submission of reports of suspected adverse reactions; Addendum I covers duplicate management.

sources.title: ICH E2D Post-approval safety data management (scientific guideline page)
sources.supports: ICH E2D (Step 5 2003, effective 2004) governs management and reporting of post-approval safety information, including reporting timeframes and follow-up; sources include patient support programmes, market research, digital media and literature.

sources.title: WHODrug Global
sources.supports: WHODrug Global is the drug dictionary used as a reference for precise drug coding.

sources.title: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2021 National Estimates
sources.supports: Mean hourly wages May 2021: medical records specialists $23.23, registered nurses $39.78, pharmacists $60.43, compliance officers $36.45, medical scientists $50.02, physicians all other $111.30.

sources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, December 2021
sources.supports: Private industry: wages 70.5% of compensation, benefits 29.5%.

assumptions: Volume, branch shares (12 percent not valid, 33 percent serious, 55 percent nonserious, 45 percent of serious cases expedited) and follow-up response rates are estimates; no published company-level distribution was opened.
Hands-on times per step are estimates; no time-and-motion study of PV case processing was opened.
Follow-up versions re-enter the serious track and are counted as further visits within one case rather than as new cases.
Occupation codes are wage proxies because pharmacovigilance roles have no dedicated SOC code.
The cycle-time benchmark is anchored on the regulatory deadline rather than a measured distribution; the long tail comes from follow-up waits.
Fte_on_process values come from hands-on time times volume at 130 productive hours a month with an allowance for reconciliation, training and audits; they include outsourced data entry staff.
Web search was limited during research, so no industry benchmark of cost per case or cases per FTE was found.
